title: Jansen linkage walker
summary: twelve legs, one keyed crankshaft, many closed loops
description: A hand-cranked twelve-legged walking machine after Theo Jansen's linkage: laser-cut birch bars and frame ribs, walnut-faced plywood triangles, brass pins and a keyed brass crankshaft, walking on a floor of boards that rolls one board per turn.

difficulty.rationale: Many coupled closed loops, flexible subassemblies, geometry-keyed configurations and a solver branch limit to navigate.

standards: DIN 125-1 A washers (M4: 4.3 x 9 x 0.8 mm)
materials: Birch plywood, 4 mm: bars, crank webs and frame ribs

motion.cycle: one crank turn; the floor rolls exactly one board, so the loop is seamless

prompt_test.model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium effort, through craft3d-cli
prompt_test.result: Built and passed: 0 dof, the reference foot within 1.25e-5 mm of the circle intersections, 4 to 6 feet on the floor, centre of mass inside the feet, slip at most 2.34 mm, no collisions at 121 moments. About 950 commands in about 130 CLI calls. It took the leg's joints from a published Jig and invented a band, a slip bound and the layer stack; these were added to the prompt afterwards, and that wording was not retested.
